title: passioncode-port-claim/1
description: DEC-0154 HA-1, DEC-0160: one OS account's port claim for one service, the file .passioncode-ports.<service>.<account>.json in the computer's shared sticky folder (/Users/Shared on macOS, /var/tmp on Linux, %ProgramData%\PassionCode\port-claims on Windows), owned by the account it names. It only keeps two installers from choosing one port and grants nothing; who may receive a credential is HA-2's check. A claim with no port is deleted, never written empty. The reference that reads, chooses and rebuilds is src/port-claim.ts (docs/specification/service.md#ha-1).

service.description: The descriptor's id; an app without a descriptor: its reverse-DNS bundle identifier, and for an app's separately recorded part that identifier plus .<part> (ai.passioncode.desktop.hub).

account.description: The OS account the claim is for: its numeric uid on macOS and Linux, its SID on Windows, never a login name (a login name can be renamed, and is not what the owner check compares). At most 100 characters, so the file name stays at or under 255 bytes.

ports.description: Every port this account's instances of the service (or the app's part) record, in one claim, at most 64. The reference rebuilds them ascending, once each (src/port-claim.ts rebuildClaim), and answers claim-invalid rather than write more; a reader takes them in any order.

updatedAt.description: When the claim was last rebuilt: interop-common's utcInstant, an RFC 3339 instant in UTC written with Z and at most three fraction digits (an offset such as +00:00, or microseconds, is refused).

bundleId.description: A reverse-DNS bundle identifier under the app's own domain, stable across versions, optionally followed by .<part>: letters, digits and hyphens in two or more dot-separated parts, at most 130 characters, so the file name (25 characters besides the service and the account) stays at or under 255 bytes.
